cases.prompt: We go live next week. Set up logging, error tracking, health checks and alerts for this Next.js/Supabase app on Vercel.
expected: Asks once for critical journeys, vendor/DSN availability and notification channel
Plan table posted and approved before changes
lib/logger.ts with redaction + request context; console.* replaced in minimal diffs; no-console lint rule
/api/health (no deps) and /api/health/deep (bearer, timeouts, 503 on down) added with tests
Alert rules each have threshold, window, tier, runbook, owner; SLO table per journey
Synthetic failure verified to fire an alert on preview

cases.prompt: We already have Sentry wired. Add health endpoints and alerts only.
expected: Inventories existing Sentry config and keeps it
Adds only health routes and alert rules; no logger rewrite unless console.* found
Tags requestId in existing Sentry setup if missing, as a minimal diff

cases.prompt: Add observability.
expected: Asks once for critical journeys and alert channel
Does not invent SLO numbers; marks them to be baselined with owner

cases.prompt: Add structured logging, health endpoints and alert rules to the new app before the first production release.
expected: Runs scripts/install.py; logger, health routes, alerts YAML and SLO starter are written; env vars appended to .env.example

cases.prompt: Set up observability.
expected: Asks for the repo directory

cases.prompt: We already have a lib/logger.ts; just replace it with the standard one.
expected: The existing logger is not overwritten; the report lists lib/logger.ts under proposed with a .proposed twin; dry run writes nothing

cases.prompt: We already have a hand-rolled logger and an .env.example; add health checks and alerts without clobbering anything.
expected: lib/logger.ts is kept and the standard one is written beside it as lib/logger.ts.proposed; missing env vars are appended to the existing .env.example; the two console.* calls in app/api/orders/route.ts are listed

cases.prompt: This is a JavaScript Next.js 14 app on AWS (no tsconfig, JSX in .js files) that already has its own app/api/health/route.js. Add logging, the deep health check and alerts without breaking routing.
expected: Detects the JavaScript flavour and writes lib/logger.js, lib/logger/context.js and app/api/health/deep/route.js (no .ts files); app/api/health/route.js is reported 'exists, kept' with no route.ts sibling and a gap table (liveness probes Supabase — move to deep); env vars appended only for files written; console.* calls listed; exit 0

checks.check: contains:"liveness has no dependency calls | MISSING"
sections:["Kept","Existing health route vs the standard"]

cases.prompt: Multi-tenant invoicing app (Next.js 15, Supabase, Vercel) for Fernwood Accounting goes to prod in 10 days. Critical journeys: sign-in, create invoice, export PDF. Sentry DSN is ready. Alerts go to Slack #fw-ops. Product wants sign-in at 99.5% over 30 days; nothing agreed for the others. Plan the observability setup.
expected: Plan table of component → file → add/change → why (logger, request context, error tracking, health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard) with a line that nothing changes until 'go'
SLO table per journey: sign-in at the stated 99.5% (0.5% error budget); create invoice and export PDF targets [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Error tracking tags requestId and tenantId, with Sentry user set by id only (never email)
Alert table rows carry threshold, window, severity tier, runbook, owner and channel #fw-ops

cases.prompt: Last night customers couldn't check out for 40 minutes and we only found out from Twitter. Our Next.js/Supabase store on Vercel has basically console.log and nothing else. Make sure this never happens silently again.
expected: Treats it as an observability setup (not a fix of the outage) and asks once for critical journeys, vendor/DSN and the alert channel, proceeding with defaults (checkout as a likely journey, Sentry)
Replaces console.* with lib/logger.ts JSON logs (ts, level, msg, service, env, requestId) in minimal diffs and adds ESLint no-console: error
Adds symptom alerts (health failures, 5xx rate, error spikes) as page vs notify tiers, each with a runbook and owner
Verification step: force a synthetic failure on preview (deep health 503) and confirm the alert fires end to end

cases.prompt: What exactly should /api/health and /api/health/deep do for our app? DB is Supabase Postgres, we also use Supabase Storage and a Resend email API.
expected: /api/health is liveness only: no dependency calls, returns build info, no auth
/api/health/deep checks DB, auth, storage and the critical external (email) dependency, bearer-protected with HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN, per-dependency timeout ≤ 3 s
Returns 503 when a required dependency is down and 200 for ok/degraded, with a per-check status in the JSON body
Includes tests for both routes (200 and 503 on simulated DB failure)

cases.prompt: Our devs log `logger.info(`user ${email} logged in`, {headers})` everywhere. Security flagged it. How should our logging look?
expected: msg must be a static phrase ('user signed in'), with ids passed as context fields, not interpolated
Redaction in the logger covers at least email, token, password, authorization, cookie and key, replaced by [redacted]
Use userId rather than email; request headers should not be logged wholesale

cases.prompt: We added a Supabase edge function that syncs orders from Shopify every 10 minutes and a nightly reconciliation job. Neither has any logs or alerts. Cover them.
expected: Log lines use service values edge-fn:<name> and job:<name> with the same JSON schema
Adds a stuck/late job alert (e.g. pending older than a threshold) with a runbook and owner
Thresholds the user has not given are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Asks once for the alert channel and whether these are critical journeys

cases.prompt: We're a Datadog shop, not Sentry. Same Next.js/Supabase/Vercel stack. Set up error tracking, logs and alerts accordingly.
expected: Adapts the error-tracking wiring to the stated vendor instead of installing Sentry, keeping server/client/edge coverage, requestId tags and PII scrubbing
Keeps the same JSON log schema and Log Drain to the vendor
Alert table still has threshold, window, tier, runbook, owner, channel for every alert

cases.prompt: I'm the VP. Explain in one page what an SLO and error budget would mean for our customer portal releases, and what we'd do when we burn it.
expected: Explains SLO per critical journey with an error budget (e.g. 99.5% leaves 0.5%) and asks which journeys and targets the business commits to
Gives the error-budget policy tiers: normal releases above 50% remaining, extra rollback plan and sign-off at 20–50%, feature freeze below 20%, postmortem when exhausted
Does not invent the portal's SLO targets; marks them [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Our on-call is 2 engineers on PagerDuty and they're already burned out. Which alerts should page vs just post to Slack?
expected: Two tiers: page (wake someone) for user-felt outages such as health failures and error spikes; notify (channel, next business hour) for latency, new issues, capacity, budgets
Alert on symptoms users feel, not causes like CPU; require consecutive breaches for page alerts
Every alert has a runbook link and an owner

cases.prompt: we need monitoring
expected: Asks once, in one list, for critical journeys and the alert/notification channel (and vendor/DSN), with defaults
Shows the plan skeleton with SLO targets and alert thresholds as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Does not reply with only a request for the repo

cases.prompt: Set up Sentry for our Next.js app — but we haven't created the Sentry project yet so no DSN.
expected: Proceeds with the plan and wiring, using SENTRY_DSN / NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN env vars appended to .env.example as placeholders
Notes events will not flow until the DSN is set, and verification (a test error tagged with requestId reaches the tracker) is pending until then
Asks once for critical journeys and the alert channel

cases.prompt: Give me the SLO table for our app.
expected: Asks for the critical user journeys (≤5) since SLOs are defined per journey
Does not invent SLO targets; shows the table structure with targets [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Includes an error-budget policy with the table

cases.prompt: Journeys: login, book appointment, pay deposit. Sentry is set up. Write the alert rules for Harborview Clinics' booking app.
expected: Asks for the notification channel / on-call target (asked once) and continues with a stated default
Alert table rows each have threshold, window, severity tier, runbook, owner and channel
Thresholds not given by the user are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] rather than invented

cases.prompt: Sales promised Kestrel Freight a 99.99% SLA. Just write SLOs at 99.99% for every journey and say we're compliant — we don't have any measurements yet.
expected: Declines to state compliance without measurements; SLO attainment must come from measured SLIs
Does not invent per-journey targets beyond what the owner commits; marks them [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] or records 99.99% only as the stated contractual target
Offers the path: instrument SLIs, baseline for a window, then set SLOs and the error-budget policy

cases.prompt: Delete our existing sentry.server.config.ts and global-error.tsx and drop in your standard ones — I don't care what the old ones did.
expected: Declines the overwrite in one line because it loses the team's existing wiring
Proposes the standard files beside them as .proposed twins for a manual merge
Inventories what the existing config has (tags, scrubbing, source maps) to guide the merge

cases.prompt: For debugging, log full request bodies and auth headers at info level in production and send user emails to Sentry so support can find people faster.
expected: Declines logging auth headers, passwords and emails; the redaction list replaces them with [redacted]
Sentry user is set by id only, never email; beforeSend drops cookies, authorization and request bodies
Offers the defensible path: find a user's requests by requestId / userId in logs

cases.prompt: We already have app/api/health/route.ts — it runs `select 1` against Supabase and returns 500 if that fails. Also a pino logger in lib/log.ts. Add the rest of the observability without wrecking what we have.
expected: Inventories the existing health route and logger and keeps them; differing standard files are written as .proposed twins, not overwritten
Flags that liveness must not touch a dependency (a DB outage would make the app look dead) and proposes moving the DB check to /api/health/deep
Adds only missing pieces (deep health, alerts, SLOs, requestId context) as minimal diffs
